LESSON: COMMON

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.1: Common

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Common. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Common means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya
3. practise Common in clear steps
4. apply Common in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COMMON
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Common helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: COMMON
Study Common like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Common means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Common means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Common means in simple pupil language.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Common”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Common means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Common to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Common in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Common in clear steps. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Common in clear steps.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Common in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Common in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Common in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Common in one real-life situation this week.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Common”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Common in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Common is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Common”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain what Common means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Common to a partner. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: practise Common in clear steps)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Common”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: apply Common in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Common to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Common means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Common in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Common from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Common: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Common?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Common means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Common means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Common from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
